The longitudinal axes of tensile and impact specimens shall be taken at a mid-radius 
location or deeper for a solid QTC or within 1/8” of the mid-wall for a hollow QTC. 
Note 4: Test temperature shall be at or below the indicated temperature. 
Note 5: Impact specimens may be taken either in the longitudinal or transverse 
orientation. 
Note 6: Impact acceptance criteria is based upon 10 mm x 10 mm specimens. 
Note 7: Toughness criteria is given in terms of the required minimum average of a seat 
of three specimens (first number) followed by the minimum value for a single specimen 
(second number). Only one specimen of a set may be below the minimum average, but 
in no case lower than the single specimen minimum.

Preheat Treat 
Machining 
If tubulars are made from trepanning barstock, the tubulars shall be heat treated after 
trepanning. Material with an ER over 8” shall be preheat treat machined to the drawing 
or EPS specified dimensions prior to heat treatment.

Furnace 
Calibration 
Heat treat furnaces used for QTC’s and production parts shall meet Equipment 
Qualifications of CMS-002.

General 
Material shall be provided in the normalized (optional), austenitize, quenched and 
tempered condition. 
Heat treating shall be done in accordance with the methods described CMS-002, 
Material Requirements for Forgings, Bars and Mill Shapes. Batch heat treating shall 
comply with the following. Cycle times apply only to temperature monitoring. 
 Method #1 - Furnace Atmosphere Thermocouple; or 
 Method #2 - Contact Surface Thermocouple. 
Method #1 - Furnace Atmosphere Thermocouple 
This method utilizes a thermocouple (T/C) that measures the temperature of the 
furnace atmosphere, but not the load itself. Holding time at temperature shall begin 
after the furnace atmosphere T/C reaches the set point temperature. Set point 
temperature must be within the allowable temperature range prescribed in the 
applicable material specification. Unless otherwise stated in the specific material 
specification, hold for the following times: 
Normalizing, Austenitizing, or Annealing: After set point temperature is reached, hold 
for a minimum of ½ hour/inch of heaviest cross section.
Cactus Wellhead Material Specification

General -

Tempering or Aging: After set point temperature is reached, hold for a minimum of 3/4
hour/inch of heaviest cross section. If a double temper is specified, the second temper 
shall be held for a minimum of ½ hour/inch of heaviest cross section. 
Method #2 - Contact Surface Thermocouple.
This method uses a T/C physically in contact with the surface of a part in the load being 
heat treated. Contact shall be made on the heaviest section of the part. Holding time 
commences after the set point temperature has been reached and shall continue for the 
minimum cycle time prescribed in the specific material specification. Set point 
temperature must be within the allowable temperature range prescribed in the 
applicable material specification. 
Method for continuous furnace – The QTC shall consist of a sacrificial length cut from the 
end of the bar and shall be from the same heat and heat treat lot as the material it qualifies.

Tempering Furnace 
 Min time 
5 minutes (Notes) 
Air cool or faster to room temperature


The bar travels through several different temperature zones which allows the bar 
to heat to an austenitic state. 

Prior to entering the tempering furnace, the bar is spray quenched. Maximum 
water temperature at start of quench is 100F (38°C). 

The tempering furnace zone temps are then selected to produce the required 
tempering effect. 

The length of the furnace and travel speed determined the time spent in the 
austenitizing and tempering furnace and the bar diameter affects the travel speed. 

To attain the required mechanical properties and microstructure, the time in each 
furnace should produce the same mechanical properties as a conventional 
quench-and-temper heat treatment.
